articles.author: Evan Gardner
articles.summary: On a spring evening in Stockton, California, Chase Ott-Wick was strolling into a bar when a stranger stopped him. The man had heard that Chase was the guy building a new data center in town—and he wanted to say: Please don’t. “He had a beautiful home that he paid for and had been living in for years, and was concerned that his view would be disrupted,” Chase told me. But as the conversation went on, he said, it became increasingly clear that what the man really feared was something bigger. “When you turn that thing on,” Chase remembers him saying, “our lives are going to change.” The people of Stockton, which is 40 miles northeast of Silicon Valley as the crow flies, worried the harsh growl of the data center would drown out the lapping sounds of the San Joaquin River; they feared the rampant water use would turn their rolling green golf courses into a sickly bed of beige; they suspected their precious populations of migratory birds and Chinook salmon would be wiped out by pollution. articles.summary: John D. “Jay” Rockefeller, the former West Virginia governor and U.S. senator born into one of the most prominent families in American history, died Friday in his Washington, D.C., home, The Washington Post reported . He was 89. The outlet did not say what caused his death. Born on June 18, 1937, weeks after his famous great-grandfather’s death, Rockefeller was a five-term Democrat senator who represented West Virginia from 1985 to 2015, and was known for pushing expansive health care and social policies and criticizing the Iraq War. He was first elected to the Senate in 1984 a fter serving as West Virginia’s secretary of state and then serving two terms as governor. In the 1990s, Rockefeller was one of the key supporters of President Bill Clinton’s failed attempt at near-universal health care coverage. He also backed former President Barack Obama’s Affordable Care Act, which was signed in 2010. Rockefeller thought Obama’s massive healthcare overhaul didn’t go far enough, and he unsuccessfully sought to make the government program available for everyone. articles.summary: Joe Camporeale / IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect/ Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports Former WWE legend Glenn Jacobs has emerged as a frontrunner to replace Tennessee Governor-elect Marsha Blackburn in the Senate, according to a new report. Two Republican officials familiar with the matter said the 59-year-old has a major advantage, citing his longstanding relationship with Blackburn. This comes after reports that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is not being considered for the soon-to-be-vacant seat. “Based on [what happened], it’s even more likely for Glenn,” one of the operatives told The Washington Sun . articles.summary: Democrats clearly had a good week, taking both the House and the Senate overwhelmingly.
